package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because its setup.py script contains a payload that performs multiple anti-analysis checks (including detection of virtual machines, sandboxes, known researcher usernames, and known researcher IP addresses). If these checks are passed, the script downloads and executes a trojan binary from an external server and exfiltrates installation results to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook. These behaviors are designed to evade detection and compromise victim systems during installation.

execution_context.trigger: install-time (execution of setup.py during package installation)
required_permissions: filesystem (to check for VM-related files and processes)
network (to make HTTP requests for IP checking, trojan download, and Discord webhook exfiltration)
environment_vars (to access system environment variables such as USERNAME)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code executes during package installation via setup.py. It first checks if the operating system is Windows, then performs anti-analysis checks by looking for the presence of virtualization software (VMware, VirtualBox), known analysis tools (vboxservice, vmtoolsd, wireshark, procmon), and known researcher usernames. It then retrieves the public IP address using wtfismyip.com and checks it against a list of known researcher IPs. If all checks are passed, it downloads and executes a trojan binary from an external server and sends a notification with installation results to a Discord webhook controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is suspicious because it is embedded in setup.py, which should only handle package installation logic. Instead, it performs extensive anti-analysis checks to evade detection by researchers and automated sandboxes. Upon passing these checks, it downloads and executes a trojan binary, which is a clear indicator of malicious intent. The exfiltration of installation results to a Discord webhook further demonstrates attacker control and intent to monitor successful compromises.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py is expected to contain only installation and configuration logic for the package. It should not perform anti-VM or anti-sandbox checks, download and execute external binaries, or exfiltrate data to external services such as Discord webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may check for virtualization environments for licensing enforcement or to optimize performance, but it is highly unusual and suspicious to combine these checks with the download and execution of trojan binaries and exfiltration of data to Discord webhooks. Legitimate use would never involve these behaviors together in an installation script.
key_indicators: Anti-VM and anti-sandbox checks in setup.py (e.g., checking for VMware/VirtualBox files and analysis tool processes)
Username and IP address filtering against known researcher values
Network request to public IP detection service (wtfismyip.com) during install
Conditional download and execution of an external trojan binary
Exfiltration of installation results to a Discord webhook
Obfuscated or conditional execution logic to evade automated analysis

attack_chain.leads_to: If all anti-analysis checks are passed, the script proceeds to the next stage.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of anti-VM or anti-sandbox checks within setup.py or other install-time scripts
Network requests to public IP detection services (e.g., wtfismyip.com) during package installation
Download and execution of external binaries from non-standard or suspicious domains at install-time
Exfiltration of installation or system information via Discord webhooks or similar messaging platforms

References to Discord webhook URLs within setup.py
References to public IP detection services such as wtfismyip.com in installation scripts

network_indicators: HTTP requests to wtfismyip.com or similar IP-checking services during installation
Outbound connections to Discord webhook endpoints (discord.com/api/webhooks/...)

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor install-time scripts (such as setup.py) for the presence of anti-analysis logic, including checks for virtualization, sandboxes, known usernames, and known IP addresses. Flag any network requests to public IP detection services or attempts to download and execute binaries from external sources during installation. Detect and alert on exfiltration attempts to Discord webhooks or other messaging platforms. Use both static analysis (to identify obfuscated or conditional payloads and suspicious references) and dynamic analysis (to observe network and process behaviors during installation) to identify these threats.
